sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud KMS: Key version states
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: a version scheduled for destruction 'can't be used for cryptographic operations' and 'can be restored to disabled during the scheduled period' (default 30 days); disabled versions keep their key material and can be re-enabled; destroyed material is removed and 'Ciphertext encrypted with a destroyed version can't be recovered'; decryption works with any enabled version. That BigQuery data written before a rotation still needs the older version, the error wording, and the key usage tracking feature are from memory of the CMEK and KMS pages (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the security engineer at Northgate Clinical Research. BigQuery datasets with trial data use the customer-managed key trial-cmek (rotated every 90 days). Yesterday a cleanup script scheduled 'old' key versions for destruction. This morning every query touching tables loaded before August fails. The quarterly safety report to the regulator is built at 10:00.
handover: The cleanup script ran as sa-key-janitor with roles/cloudkms.admin on the key ring.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the key's versions and their states, and the tables whose data each version protects.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

secops@cloudshell:~$ for v in 1 2; do gcloud kms keys versions restore $v --key trial-cmek --keyring trials --location europe-west2 && gcloud kms keys versions enable $v --key trial-cmek --keyring trials --location europe-west2; done

guard.label: Take destroy rights from the janitor (disable only), make it check key usage first, and alert on any DestroyCryptoKeyVersion

secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud kms keyrings remove-iam-policy-binding trials ... --member serviceAccount:sa-key-janitor@... --role roles/cloudkms.admin; add-iam-policy-binding ... --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersionManager-disable-only (custom)

writeup.question: For the record: why pre-August data was unreadable, what you restored and why it was still possible, and what stops it recurring.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Rotation made version 3 primary in August, but older data is still protected through versions 1 and 2. The janitor scheduled both for destruction yesterday, so BigQuery could not decrypt pre-August partitions.

parts.label: Restored
parts.modelAnswer: Versions scheduled for destruction can be restored to disabled within the period (here until mid-December), then enabled. Destroyed versions could not have been. Granting KMS admin to the service agent would not have helped.

parts.label: Recurrence
parts.modelAnswer: The janitor now can only disable, checks key usage first, and any DestroyCryptoKeyVersion alerts security.

expertPath.text: Versions 1-2 DESTROY_SCHEDULED; error names v2's state; janitor did it at 17:02; its rule ignores data use.
Restore and enable 1 and 2; limit the janitor; usage check; alert.

agentAdmin.headline: Not a permission problem
agentAdmin.body: The error named a key version's state. The fix is restoring the versions within their scheduled period; widening permissions only weakens separation of duties.

filingLate.headline: Rotation keeps old versions in use
filingLate.body: Rotation creates a new primary for new data; older data still needs the older versions. A version scheduled for destruction can be restored; one destroyed cannot.

restored.headline: Good: caught it inside the window
restored.body: You read the versions' states and the error, saw the destruction was still only scheduled, restored and enabled them, checked every quarter, and took destruction rights away from automation.

scoring.modelReasoning: Queries fail because the key versions that protect pre-August data are scheduled for destruction; rotation made a new primary but old data still needs the old versions. They are only scheduled, so restore them (to disabled) and enable them, then check every quarter. More KMS rights for BigQuery do not fix a version's state and weaken separation of duties. Then stop the automation from destroying versions and alert on destruction.
